c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: There is no "turn" block for a curve. So how does the Cutebot turn?

A.text: The two wheels run at different speeds

B.text: The body tilts to one side

D.text: The car lifts one wheel off the floor

c1.why: A difference in wheel speed is a turn. The bigger the difference, the tighter the curve.

c2.label: Q2
c2.why: A millisecond is a thousandth of a second, so 1000 of them make one second.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: While a `pause` block is running, what are the wheels doing?

B.text: Carrying on at their last speed

c3.why: `pause` holds the program, not the motors. The wheels keep whatever they were last told.

r1.label: Q1
r1.prompt: Which way does the car curve?
r1.why: The left wheel is faster than the right, so the car swings around the slower side — to the right.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: What shape does the car draw?

B.text: A short straight, then a curve

r2.why: Read it top to bottom: straight for a fifth of a second, then it curves — and keeps curving, because nothing stops the wheels.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: What does the car do over and over?
r3.why: The two speed pairs are mirror images, so the car leans one way and then the other — the two loops of a figure eight.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: How much of a right-hand curve does the car actually make?

C.text: Almost none — the next block replaces it immediately

D.text: None — the two blocks cancel out

r4.why: With no pause between them, the second speed pair arrives at once. A speed with no time after it is a speed the car barely uses.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: This was meant to be a figure eight, but the car only ever leans one way. Which change fixes it?

C.text: Put the pauses before the motor blocks

d1.why: `100, 100` is straight, so only one curve is left. A figure eight needs a curve each way — one pair mirroring the other.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: The car never dances — it just keeps circling one way. What is missing?

D.text: Pauses between the two speed pairs

d2.why: Without a pause the second pair replaces the first at once, so the car nearly always runs 40, 100 and circles one way. Each speed pair needs its own pause.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Put one loop of the figure eight in order: 1 pause 1000 · 2 motors 100 40 · 3 pause 200 · 4 forward
b1.why: A short straight to enter the loop, then the curve held for a second. Each move needs its own pause after it.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: Which pair of blocks makes the tightest curve?
b2.why: The slower the slow wheel is compared with the fast one, the tighter the turn — 60, 0 is tighter than 100, 40 even though both gaps are 60. With one wheel stopped, the car pivots around it.
